question: Should existing platform-prefixed generic target values remain valid inputs, or is this PR intentionally making a breaking address-contract change?
rationale: The new encoding removes collisions but changes the normalized identity of configurations accepted by the existing codec, and the permanent compatibility contract cannot be inferred safely from tests alone.

options.title: Preserve legacy inputs
options.body: Recognize existing canonical addresses while using an unambiguous versioned encoding for new raw channel and thread components.

options.title: Accept the breaking change
options.body: Land the new interpretation only with explicit upgrade documentation, migration guidance, and tests proving the intended operator impact.

options.title: Pause for codec redesign
options.body: Hold the PR until a single versioned address grammar covers encoding, decoding, and migration without heuristic ambiguity.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy inputs
recommendation.body: Recognize existing canonical addresses while using an unambiguous versioned encoding for new raw channel and thread components.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the three coordinated commits and are the strongest available person to explain whether the address-contract change is deliberate.
